page.layout: One printed page: heading "DEDICATORIA." at top, then running dedicatory text in full width, a centred two-line verse-like motto, a centred signature line. A partial column of text runs along the left edge of the scan (the facing page's margin, cut off), not transcribed as it is the neighbouring page's edge.

l.i: Sed facile sentio, quā tuis virtutibus non modo
assentatorij stylifuco exaggerandis, sed vel sim-
plici dictione commemorandis, nostra ieiuna ora-
tio in pingues & nitentes oratorum campos nun-
quam admissa impar fit. Ignosce quaso (generose
Comes) insigni huic temeritati te tam audaciter
appellare audæ & (quod vnum à te & petimus, &
pro tua summa humanitate expectamus) hanc of-
ficiosam gratulationem, ab animo tuæ virtutis,
quam sui commodi magis studioso profectam ex-
istima. Deus te ecclesiæ suæ tuaq; & patriæ et
principi incolumem, veraque virtutis gloria floren-
tissimum seruet. Londini anno salutis reue-
latæ sesquimillesimo nonagesimo sexto, octauo ca-

main_text.l: Qui tuas virtutes omni amore & admiratione

page.notes: Partly illegible or doubtful words in the italic passage (e.g. "audæ", "tuaq;", "amplici") are as read from the scan. The left-edge fragments belong to the adjacent page and were omitted. The motto and signature are set in roman type, centred.
